stories.headline: Nvidia restarts H200 production for China, Beijing approves sales, Groq chips also planned

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026 on March 17, Jensen Huang announced Nvidia has received purchase orders from Chinese customers and is restarting H200 manufacturing, stating: 'We have received purchase orders from many customers and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing.'
key_facts.excerpt: We have received purchase orders from many customers and we're in the process of restarting our manufacturing.

key_facts.fact: Chinese authorities approved multiple companies to purchase H200 chips, Nvidia's second-most powerful AI processors, according to Reuters on March 18.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese authorities have approved multiple companies to purchase H200 chips, Nvidia's second-most powerful AI processors.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is also manufacturing specialized Groq AI chips for the Chinese market, expected to be available in May 2026, according to Reuters sources.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia is manufacturing specialized Groq artificial-intelligence chips for the Chinese market, expected available in May.

key_facts.fact: Huang noted the situation changed recently: at CES in January he was still awaiting purchase orders. As of late February, 'a small number of H200 products' had been approved but Nvidia had 'yet to generate any revenue' from China.
key_facts.excerpt: Our supply chain is getting fired up.

key_facts.fact: Huang previously forecast at least $1 trillion in chip orders through 2027, and with Groq 3 LPU additions suggested: 'Theoretically, that $1 trillion could become $1.25 trillion.'
key_facts.excerpt: Theoretically, that $1 trillion could become $1.25 trillion.

stories.headline: China's No. 2 chipmaker Hua Hong readies 7nm production for AI chips with Huawei support

key_facts.fact: Hua Hong Group, China's second-largest chip manufacturer, has developed a 7-nanometre production process for AI chips, making it the second Chinese chipmaker after SMIC to achieve this capability.
key_facts.excerpt: Hua Hong, the second-biggest chip manufacturer in mainland China, has developed a 7-nanometre production process that can be used to make AI chips.

key_facts.fact: Hua Hong's contract chipmaking unit Huali Microelectronics is preparing to deploy the new process at its Shanghai facility (Fab 6), with plans for initial production capacity of a few thousand wafers per month by end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Huali Microelectronics, is preparing to deploy the new process at its Shanghai facility... a few thousand wafers per month by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: Huawei Technologies collaborated on the new 7nm technology through domestic partners, including SiCarrier, a chip equipment maker backed by Huawei.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei Technologies... has been in co... The company supported development through domestic partners, including SiCarrier—a chip equipment maker backed by Huawei.

key_facts.fact: AI chip designer Biren is reportedly using the process for a product at the prototype stage. Fab 6 currently produces chips using older 22nm and 28nm technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: AI chip designer Biren is reportedly using the process for a product at the prototype stage.

sources.title: Exclusive: China's No. 2 chipmaker readies 7 nm production as Beijing ramps up self-sufficiency drive
China's Hua Hong Develops 7nm Process For AI Chips

stories.headline: Samsung to manufacture Nvidia's Groq 3 LPU chip on 4nm process, first Nvidia chip since 2020

key_facts.fact: Samsung Foundry will produce Nvidia's Groq 3 LPU using its 4nm SF4X process node, with expected shipment in Q3 2026. This is Samsung's first Nvidia chip since manufacturing RTX 3000 series GPUs in 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Foundry will produce Groq 3 chips using its 4nm (SF4X) process node. Expected shipment: Q3 2026.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang thanked Samsung at GTC 2026: 'I want to thank Samsung, who manufactures the Groq 3 LPU chip for us. They are working as hard as they can, and I really appreciate it.'
key_facts.excerpt: I want to thank Samsung, who manufactures the Groq 3 LPU chip for us. They are working as hard as they can, and I really appreciate it.

key_facts.fact: Each Groq 3 LPU contains 98 billion transistors, 500 MB of on-chip SRAM, and delivers 150 TB/s bandwidth — approximately 7x more bandwidth than Nvidia's Rubin platform with HBM memory.
key_facts.excerpt: Chip specifications: 500MB SRAM, 98 billion transistors, 150TB/s bandwidth.

key_facts.fact: The deal represents Samsung's return as an Nvidia foundry partner after a six-year gap, having lost the contract when Nvidia switched exclusively to TSMC after the RTX 3000 generation.
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung previously manufactured Nvidia's RTX 3000 series GPUs in 2020 but lost the contract when Nvidia switched exclusively to TSMC.

sources.title: Samsung starts making Groq 3 LPU chips for Nvidia
Nvidia GTC 2026: Jensen Huang projects US$1 trillion inference market, LPU chip to be made by Samsung

stories.headline: Micron enters high-volume production of HBM4 memory and PCIe Gen6 SSDs for Nvidia Vera Rubin

key_facts.fact: At GTC 2026 on March 17, Micron Technology announced it has entered high-volume production of HBM4 memory and PCIe Gen6 SSDs purpose-built for Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin AI platform.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron Technology signaled a major push in the AI hardware race, announcing high-volume production of memory and storage components purpose-built for Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin ecosystem.

key_facts.fact: The announcement represents a critical milestone as memory and storage are becoming the key infrastructure bottleneck for next-generation AI computing platforms, with HBM4 offering significantly higher bandwidth than previous HBM generations.
key_facts.excerpt: A major push in the AI hardware race.

key_facts.fact: Micron had previously set 2026 as the target year for HBM4 mass production, and this GTC announcement confirms the company has hit that milestone on schedule.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron Technology announced it has entered high-volume production.

sources.title: Micron enters high-volume production of HBM4 and PCIe Gen6 SSDs for Nvidia platforms

stories.headline: Meta accelerates custom AI chip rollout with Broadcom four-generation ASIC design deal

key_facts.fact: Meta announced plans to launch four generations of custom ASIC product lines over the next two years: MTIA 300 (already mass-produced), MTIA 400, MTIA 450, and MTIA 500, all primarily targeting AI inference workloads.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta recently announced plans to launch four generations of ASIC product lines over the next two years, including the already mass-produced MTIA 300 and upcoming MTIA 400, 450, and 500 chips.

key_facts.fact: Broadcom has secured a multi-generation chip design deal with Meta covering four generations of development, reflecting the industry trend of major tech companies accelerating custom silicon to reduce dependence on Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: Broadcom has secured a multi-generation chip design deal with Meta, covering four generations of development.

key_facts.fact: MediaTek is also involved in Meta's 2nm ASIC projects, alongside Google's expanding ASIC capabilities, signaling a broader industry push toward custom AI silicon.
key_facts.excerpt: MediaTek's involvement in Meta's 2nm ASIC projects and mentions Google's expanding ASIC capabilities.

sources.title: Meta accelerates AI ASIC roll-out as Broadcom secures four-generation chip design deal

stories.headline: Iran war threatens global chip supply as Strait of Hormuz blockade enters third week

key_facts.fact: The US-Iran conflict and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz since March 4, 2026 is threatening the global semiconductor industry, as Taiwan — which manufactures roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips through TSMC — relies on imported energy flowing through the strait.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwan, which manufactures roughly 90% of the world's most advanced semiconductors through TSMC alone, runs on imported energy, and a significant chunk of that energy flows through the Strait.

key_facts.fact: The Middle East supplies 37% of the fuel powering Taiwan's electric grid via LNG imports. Qatar, Iran's maritime neighbor, accounts for about one-third of the world's helium supply, which Taiwan imports and is essential for semiconductor production with no viable alternatives.
key_facts.excerpt: The Middle East supplies 37% of the fuel that powers Taiwan's electric grid... Qatar accounts for about one-third of the world's helium supply... Helium is essential for heat management during semiconductor production.

key_facts.fact: TSMC shares have fallen about 7% since the war began, versus a roughly 6% decline in global stocks. TSMC stated it 'does not anticipate any significant impact currently' and will continue monitoring the situation.
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC shares have fallen about 7% since the war began... TSMC said it does not anticipate any significant impact currently.

key_facts.fact: South Korea has warned the conflict could disrupt supply of key chipmaking materials, as the semiconductor industry faces mounting threats that the conflict will choke off key supplies and spike power costs in Taiwan.
key_facts.excerpt: The global semiconductor industry is facing mounting threats the U.S.-Iran conflict will choke off key supplies vital for chipmaking and spike the cost of power in Taiwan.

sources.title: Iran war choke-points begin to cast doubt on global chip supply
US-Iran War Is Threatening Taiwan And The World's Chip Supply

stories.headline: Galbot humanoid robot plays real-time tennis with humans using LATENT system from Tsinghua/Peking

key_facts.fact: Galbot Robotics released a video on March 16 showing a Unitree G1 humanoid robot rallying tennis shots with a human player in real time, using the LATENT system (Learning Athletic Humanoid Tennis Skills from Imperfect Human Motion Data).
key_facts.excerpt: Galbot Robotics has released a video on its official X handle on March 16 showing a humanoid robot rallying tennis shots with a human player in real time.

key_facts.fact: The LATENT system was developed by Galbot in collaboration with Tsinghua University and Peking University. It represents the first real-time whole-body planning and control algorithm for athletic humanoid tennis.
key_facts.excerpt: The demonstration showcases the company's LATENT system, developed in collaboration with researchers from Tsinghua University and Peking University.

key_facts.fact: Researchers collected just five hours of motion data from five players capturing essential movements on a compact 3x5-meter court (17 times smaller than regulation), achieving a 96% forehand success rate in simulation tests.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers collected five hours of motion data from five players... 96% success rate for forehand shots in simulation tests.

key_facts.fact: The robot demonstrated millisecond-level reaction times, precise ball striking, and natural whole-body motion during sustained rallies, consistently returning balls to the opponent's court.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, a humanoid robot can sustain high-dynamic, long-horizon tennis rallies with millisecond-level reactions, precise ball striking.

sources.title: Humanoid robot plays tennis with humans, returns fast shots in real time

stories.headline: Gecko Robotics wins $71M Navy contract for AI-powered wall-climbing ship inspection robots

key_facts.fact: The U.S. Navy and GSA awarded Gecko Robotics a $71 million contract to use wall-climbing robots and AI to inspect ships, jets, and other military assets, with any DoD branch eligible to use the technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Navy and GSA will pay Gecko Robotics $71 million to use its drones and AI to inspect ships, jets, and other gear.

key_facts.fact: Gecko's robots can identify repairs up to 50 times faster and more accurately than human inspectors, and can assess ships before they reach dry dock, enabling the Navy to pre-position personnel and parts.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says it can identify repairs up to 50 times faster and more accurately than human inspectors.

key_facts.fact: The contract covers destroyers, amphibious warships, littoral combat ships, aircraft carriers, and submarines. At any given time, approximately 52 of the Navy's ~290 battle-force ships are undergoing repairs.
key_facts.excerpt: Approximately 52 of the Navy's ~290 battle-force ships are undergoing repairs.

key_facts.fact: The Navy aims to reach 80% fleet readiness by 2027, up from only 41% of ships completing repairs on time in 2025 against a 71% target. NAVSEA's commander set revised 2026 goals 'north of 60 percent.'
key_facts.excerpt: Only 41 percent of ships completed repairs on time in 2025, falling short of the 71-percent target.

sources.title: US Navy to use wall-climbing robots to inspect ships

stories.headline: Foundation's Phantom MK-1 humanoid soldier robots deployed to Ukraine for battlefield testing

key_facts.fact: Two Phantom MK-1 humanoid robots developed by San Francisco startup Foundation were delivered to Ukraine in February 2026 for testing near the front line in reconnaissance and surveillance roles.
key_facts.excerpt: Two humanoid robots designed for military operations have been deployed to Ukraine for battlefield evaluation... known as the Phantom MK-1, were developed by the San Francisco robotics startup Foundation.

key_facts.fact: The robots stand approximately 5 feet 9 inches tall, weigh 175-180 pounds, and are designed to operate standard military hardware and equipment built for human use.
key_facts.excerpt: Height: Approximately 5 feet 9 inches. Weight: 175-180 pounds. Designed to operate standard military hardware and equipment built for human use.

key_facts.fact: The robots use camera-based vision, proprietary cycloid actuators providing high torque with quiet operation, and a 'human in the loop' control model where operators retain authority over critical decisions.
key_facts.excerpt: Human in the loop control model where robots handle autonomous navigation while operators retain authority over critical decisions.

key_facts.fact: Foundation aims to manufacture up to 50,000 robots by 2027, with an estimated annual leasing cost of approximately $100,000 per unit. Current roles include surveillance, bomb disposal, and logistics support.
key_facts.excerpt: Foundation aims to manufacture up to 50,000 robots by 2027, with an estimated annual leasing cost of approximately $100,000 per unit.

stories.headline: Kepler commissions first NVIDIA-powered cloud computing across 10-satellite orbital constellation

key_facts.fact: Kepler Communications announced the successful commissioning of distributed on-orbit computing across its Tranche 1 optical data relay constellation on March 16, transitioning its network from a data transport layer into a scalable cloud-native processing environment in orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: Kepler Communications announced the successful commissioning of distributed on-orbit computing across its Tranche 1 optical data relay constellation.

key_facts.fact: The 'Kepler Compute' fabric is powered by 40 NVIDIA Jetson Orin modules deployed as distributed edge GPUs across 10 satellites in the Tranche 1 'Aether' series, launched in January 2026 on SpaceX Falcon 9, with terabytes of SSD-based onboard storage.
key_facts.excerpt: The Kepler Compute fabric is powered by 40 NVIDIA Jetson Orin modules, deployed as distributed edge GPUs across the ten satellites that make up the Tranche 1 Aether series.

key_facts.fact: CEO Mina Mitry stated: 'By leveraging NVIDIA AI infrastructure in our optical network, data can be processed, routed, and acted on in orbit rather than waiting to return to Earth.' Applications include real-time wildfire detection, maritime anomaly sensing, and autonomous sensor retasking.
key_facts.excerpt: By leveraging NVIDIA AI infrastructure in our optical network, data can be processed, routed, and acted on in orbit rather than waiting to return to Earth.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia also announced the Vera Rubin Space Module at GTC, delivering up to 25x more AI compute than H100 for space applications. Six partners are adopting NVIDIA space platforms: Kepler, Axiom Space, Planet Labs, Aetherflux, Sophia Space, and Starcloud.
key_facts.excerpt: Vera Rubin Space Module delivers up to 25x more AI compute for space-based inferencing compared to NVIDIA H100 GPU.

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang declared: 'Space computing, the final frontier, has arrived. AI processing across space and ground systems enables real-time sensing, decision-making and autonomy.' Kepler plans Tranche 2 launch for early 2028 with 100-gigabit optical links.
key_facts.excerpt: Space computing, the final frontier, has arrived.

stories.headline: Didi unveils R2 mass-produced robotaxi with 33-sensor suite and thermal imaging for L4 autonomy

key_facts.fact: Didi Autonomous Driving unveiled the R2, its next-generation mass-produced robotaxi co-developed with GAC Aion, featuring Raytron's automotive thermal camera as a key component of its 33-sensor perception system.
key_facts.excerpt: Didi Autonomous Driving has unveiled the R2, its next-generation mass-produced robotaxi co-developed with GAC Aion, featuring Raytron's automotive thermal camera as a key component of its perception system.

key_facts.fact: The R2 integrates 33 sensors including thermal imaging into a 360-degree blind-spot-free perception architecture, enabling reliable detection in low-light and adverse weather conditions where standard cameras and LiDAR encounter limitations.
key_facts.excerpt: Integrated alongside a sophisticated suite of 33 sensors, Raytron's thermal imaging helps complete a 360° blind-spot-free perception architecture.

key_facts.fact: The thermal camera addresses critical gaps in L4 autonomous driving where visible-light cameras can be compromised by strong backlighting, sudden transitions between light and dark environments, or heavy rain and fog.
key_facts.excerpt: Visible-light cameras can be compromised by the strong backlighting... In the complex landscape of urban mobility, standard sensors often encounter invisible barriers.

sources.title: Didi Autonomous Driving Partners with Raytron to Deploy Thermal Imaging in Next-Gen Robotaxi
